page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

The x86_64 architecture of the Xeon processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8) for matrix math, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. Total Memory Encryption (TME) is also active.

In benchmark testing, the c8i.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core Geekbench scores and text processing, both placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show strong performance in the top 25%. Multi-core operations, including stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the average tier. Small-model LLM inference text generation (135M model) is highly efficient at 348.03 tokens per second, though larger 7B model inference speeds remain average.

The instance provides a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for workloads requiring high clock speeds and advanced vector or matrix instructions without the overhead of local storage. It is suited for batch processing, web serving, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight machine learning inference. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, making it less suitable for heavy database or large-scale deep learning workloads.
